category_title: Nonverbal students with ASD who engage in repetitive tapping or premature screen advancing during iPad-based instruction
student_description: This student is predominantly nonverbal with ASD and engages in repetitive, stereotypical movements (rapid swiping, tapping) when using an iPad independently. They uniquely require direct, active physical or visual guidance (like hand-over-hand prompting or modeling) and a dedicated communication partner to ensure technology is used for its intended educational or communicative purpose rather than self-stimulation.

criteria.rationale: Over time, the student needs systematic instruction to reduce reliance on hand-over-hand prompting and decrease stereotypical device use.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate specific, research-based instructional procedures such as time delay, differential reinforcement, or stimulus prompting and fading.

criteria.rationale: Because the student engages in repetitive movements on the iPad, mixing academic/leisure apps with communication apps compromises their ability to communicate effectively.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must establish a system that separates communication from other functions, such as providing a dedicated, separate device solely for AAC use.
